quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When it is raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the road is very slippery. Oil from cars hasn't washed away yet. It is safest to ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: You should keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. In bad weather or other poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow to warn the other driver.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. This warns them so they see you slowing down and any hazards ahead.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: You are able to see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
There is pleasant and clear weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when traffic is heavy. Also increase it in bad weather, at night, or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what is the safest way?

options.text: By proceeding straight within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: By proceeding straight within your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle can push you into another lane and is dangerous.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time and apply extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but mainly focus on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. You need good traction to swerve safely. Do one action first, then do the other.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Counterbalance the leaning motorcycle by keeping their body upright.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and the turn.
Counterbalance their leaning body by keeping the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Counterbalance the leaning motorcycle by keeping their body upright.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. But in slow, tight turns, keep your body upright to balance the leaning motorcycle.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: You should wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from injuries and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should NOT be used?

options.text: Plan travel distances based on the least experienced rider's ability.
Skip breaks so riders can reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders can reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan trip distances based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce tiredness. Place new riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation to be safe.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This area is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually provides enough grip for safe riding. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can often ride beside it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake hard while slowly increasing front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Fatigue while riding can be increased by:

options.text: Riding in cool, windy, or rainy weather.
Starting your ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool, windy, or rainy weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from bad weather like wind and rain, which cause tiredness. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may get very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If rain starts while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil that makes it slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Squeeze the front brake hard to prevent the front tire from locking.
Use either brake, but use only one at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use light pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have rounded, curved mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars look closer than they really are.
Show only a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They also make objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to curved mirrors.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard on the road
questions.explanation: Group riding signals help riders communicate. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard in the roadway on the right side.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the handlebars and stop.
questions.explanation: When you must stop quickly in a curve, straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten up, apply the brakes smoothly. Lean less, then brake harder as you slow down.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so other drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with the rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing can guarantee that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will. Stay alert and defensive.

questions.question: What should you do when taking a long trip?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold and wind.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold and wind.
questions.explanation: On long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a rest break at least every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants, as the crash when they wear off causes worse fatigue.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group riding into a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for a group to stay close while keeping safe spacing. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.
